contributes_to.justification: The PKB store's own git repository is the durability substrate under every node in the graph. A repo that cannot repack and cannot self-repair is an integrity defect that ends in stranded writes, which is how this failure has already presented three times.

The 1.1 GB unrepackable pack sits on the same host and the same I/O path as the write latency Nic is asking to feel fixed, and its sidecar OOM stranded writes on the morning the goal was set. A faster build shipped onto a repo that still cannot repack ships onto a substrate that is still degrading.

nodes.consequence: The PKB repo's 1.1 GB pack is now permanent by configuration: `gc.auto 0` stops it re-killing the sync sidecar, and also stops it ever repairing itself. The pack only grows. When it next outgrows whatever memory limit is in force, the sync loop starts failing every 60 seconds again and writes strand in the container exactly as they did on 2026-08-13 and, before that, on 2026-04-17 and 2026-04-03. The failure is silent by construction — the repeating repack failure was the only symptom anyone ever saw, and nobody saw it for three days. Raising the memory limit bought time and removed the alarm; it did not fix the growth.

nodes.consequence: A user who types `--dry-run` to see what WOULD happen has their PKB written to instead. The flag is the standard way to ask for a preview before a destructive operation, so this defect fires precisely when someone is being careful, and it fires silently — the command prints "Canvas synced back to PKB." and exits 0. Writes land in markdown frontmatter across the brain via sync_diff_to_disk with no confirmation step and no undo. The same command name honours the flag over MCP, so a user who has learned the safe behaviour there carries a false expectation to the CLI. Introduced 2026-08-18 by 7bed99c and unmerged, so the blast radius is currently anyone running the binary from branch `tweaks`.

Email MCP mislabels Brisbane local time as UTC — `messages_get` stamps `+00:00` on AEST values while `messages_search` stamps `+10:00` on the same message; every graph timestamp sourced this way is off by ten hours
nodes.consequence: This silently corrupts every date the graph learns from email. Timestamps captured through this path are Brisbane wall-clock wearing a UTC label, so any downstream comparison against a real UTC instant — deadline arithmetic, "was this before or after that", cross-source reconciliation — is wrong by ten hours, and wrong in a direction that looks plausible. It has already written bad data: task_f1f59685's consequence field cites an editor email at "2026-08-08 03:55" that is in fact 03:55 Brisbane. Because two tools on the same server disagree about the same message, a reader has no way to tell which convention any given recorded timestamp followed, so historical captures cannot be corrected by rule — only by re-reading the source. Every day this stands adds more uncorrectable records.

A worker instructed to "branch from origin/dev" — the literal wording of these briefs — cannot detect that it did not. Consequences: (a) PRs are built on arbitrary stale bases and may reintroduce reverted code or conflict on merge; (b) in-container findings about "what is on dev" are silently invalidated, because the worker read a different tree than the name implies; (c) a defect already fixed upstream will be re-found, re-filed and re-fixed. At the time of the v7.3 self-test the gap was 8 commits. It is unbounded in general: it equals however far the shared host checkout has drifted, which no dispatcher checks and no worker can see.

In the measured session, 60 of 248 `pkb__get_task` calls were a different agent re-fetching an id another agent in the same wave had already fetched — 659 KB, 32.1% of that tool's bytes, for material the wave already held. It scales with fan-out, so it gets worse exactly as the framework leans harder on parallel workers: the same 73-subagent shape at twice the width doubles the duplicated bytes without doing more work. nodes.consequence: The doctrine as merged is self-defeating: it tells every spawner to name every child, and a named child is a teammate that cannot name children of its own — so the instruction reaches its own level and throws at the next. contributes_to.justification: This target's efficiency branch states the bar directly — 'rebuilds and writes don't block sessions'. Today writes block sessions for up to 180 s and sometimes strand. This is the write-side of that target, and the integrity branch is engaged too because an untrustworthy write return is an integrity defect, not a speed one.

This is the headline deliverable of Nic's end-of-week goal. The goal's acceptance test is this task's p95 number, observed by hand against the deployed build. If this does not land, the goal is not met by any other route.

nodes.consequence: The PKB is the framework's only memory and every agent is required to write to it. At today's cost a single node write serialises 333.8 MB, and writes have been observed timing out at 180 s, returning unreliable results in both directions, and stranding without applying. That does not merely slow work down — it makes the memory substrate something Nic and every agent route around, which is the failure mode the whole PKB exists to prevent. Nic has already stated the threshold at which he stops using it.

nodes.label: PROBE 1: ida (WSL, Discord-connected) → in-session team of `james` agents → each driving synchronous polecats to done
nodes.consequence: This is the arrangement that needs no new infrastructure — everything it uses ships today. If it works, the other two are optimisations rather than requirements. If it fails, it fails on a rule that is already documented, and the failure tells us the shipped framework cannot express the topology its own design assumes.

nodes.label: PROBE 2: ida (WSL, Discord-connected) → separate-process `james` on WSL → agy polecats → cross-session messaging back to ida
nodes.consequence: This arrangement is the only one of the three that escapes the flat-roster ceiling, because a separate process is not a teammate of ida's. If it works, it is the shape the framework should be built around. If addressability turns out to cost the ability to name workers, then no arrangement in the current harness can be both supervised and hierarchical, and that is a design constraint Nic needs stated rather than discovered later.

nodes.label: PROBE 3: ida (WSL, Discord-connected) → `james` in an ISOLATED CONTAINER → agy headless agents doing the work → cross-session messaging back to ida
nodes.consequence: This is the arrangement that would let untrusted or long-running work proceed without a host session babysitting it. It is also the one with the most stacked prior negatives: headless agy auto-denies everything and reports SUCCESS while doing so, a containerised coordinator cannot launch further containers, and no message has ever been observed crossing the container boundary into a host session. If those hold, the arrangement is not viable today and the epic should say so plainly rather than leaving it as an aspiration on the map.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Make the graph earn its keep: chain slack, unlock breadth, value lineage, and retire the one genuinely dead signal

Until this lands, the doctrine that agents express importance via contributes_to rather than priority bands is a doctrine that routes importance into the weakest signal in the model.

nodes.label: Seed-verification retry is dead code — the cidfile is cleared before the retry loop, so attempt 2 always dies at docker exit 125
nodes.consequence: Polecat advertises a 2-attempt seed-verification retry and has none. Attempt 2 cannot start a container, so any transient seeding failure — the exact class the retry exists to absorb — is fatal on the first try. Worse, the diagnostic is actively misleading: the failure message reports `last exit=125`, which is docker refusing to start because a cidfile already exists, not the agent's real exit code. Anyone debugging a failed dispatch is handed the retry's own artifact as if it were the worker's verdict, and the true attempt-1 failure is buried.

nodes.consequence: If PKB writes are unreliable, every agent action is unverifiable, data drift accumulates silently, and scoring and triage operate on lies. The entire framework's reliance on PKB state as ground truth becomes fiction.

nodes.label: Target: Peer review obligations delivered on time

contributes_to.justification: Peer-review service sustains standing with ARC panels and editorial boards — one recurring axis of the World-Class Academic Profile goal among several (publications, teaching, grants).

nodes.consequence: Late or poor-quality reviews damage standing with ARC panels and journal editorial boards. Reduces future assessor invitations and editorial trust. Reputational cost within the research community — recoverable but compounds if it becomes a pattern.

nodes.label: Target: Professional courtesy — prompt, polite responses to loose contacts

contributes_to.justification: Being approachable and professionally responsive across the wider network sustains the reputation and reach that the Impact & Engagement goal depends on; courtesy to loose contacts is a diffuse but real contributor.

nodes.consequence: Small reputational cost from being slow or impolite to people Nic doesn't know well but should treat professionally — loose contacts, one-off enquiries, peripheral correspondents. No single lapse matters much, but a pattern of brusqueness or silence quietly erodes a reputation for being approachable and professional.

nodes.label: Target: Prospective HDR candidates get a timely, professional response

contributes_to.justification: A healthy HDR supervision pipeline feeds the future capacity and standing of the research programme (the world-class-profile goal); responsiveness to candidates is a meaningful but not singular input to that goal.

nodes.consequence: A slow or absent reply to a prospective HDR candidate loses good candidates to other supervisors and carries a minor reputational cost — promising students judge a prospective supervisor partly on responsiveness, and silence reads as disinterest.

nodes.label: Target: Publish high-quality scholarly papers in prestigious open-access outlets

contributes_to.justification: High-contribution to academic-profile (publications are the single most legible signal in fellowship/promotion/standing assessments) with low aggregation risk (the profile goal spans publications + teaching + grants + collaborations; publications is one major axis but not the sole pathway).

nodes.consequence: If the publication pipeline silts up — a year or two without substantive papers landing in venues the field actually reads — fellowship contention, PhD-supervision pipelines, invited roles, and policy-influence channels all decay together. The damage is slow and compounding rather than acute: each individual missed paper is forgivable, the accumulated absence is not, and academic credibility erodes into a consulting voice.

nodes.label: Target: Research compliance obligations met (ethics, reporting, governance)

contributes_to.justification: Clean, current research compliance is close to a precondition for a credible active research programme — a suspended approval halts the research the world-class-profile goal is built on, so this target is a strong (but not sole) contributor to that goal.

nodes.consequence: A missed ethics/compliance deadline can suspend an approval and halt active data collection that a CI team depends on — a serious, hard-to-recover consequence. Compliance failures cascade: a suspended approval stops research, exposes co-investigators, and damages institutional standing in a way that takes far longer to rebuild than the original obligation took to meet.

nodes.label: Target: TJA paper v1 submitted

contributes_to.justification: TJA paper submission is a direct contribution to the scholarly output target — novel empirical work on trans journalism standards evaluation.

Working journalists rarely read academic papers directly; the paper reaches the newsroom channel only indirectly (via coverage or the website built on its findings). Uncertain potential impact — modelled now, low confidence.

nodes.consequence: (opportunity cost) Miss the publication window while the TJA finding is salient; benchmarking work remains orphaned; slip to 2027 reduces impact and weakens the downstream research program's narrative.

nodes.consequence: Miss the window of political salience for trans rights journalism while the TJA work is directly relevant; public impact of the research goes unrealised; the fellowship case loses its most visible proof point — a live, usable public artefact demonstrating research translation, not just publications.

nodes.consequence: Fire-and-forget dispatch on the interactive path never terminates and never produces its own run record — the two properties fire-and-forget most needs. Every interactive dispatch therefore requires a human to notice it, judge it done, and kill it by hand.

The seed-failure path structurally CANNOT preserve the workspace: `fail()` exits before `preserve_workspace` is ever set, so the one failure most worth inspecting is the one always deleted
nodes.consequence: Any interactive polecat run ended by `docker stop` deterministically loses its workspace. The `preserve_workspace` mechanism added for exactly this purpose is unreachable on the seed-failure path: `fail()` raises `SystemExit` out of the RHS of the `returncode` assignment, so control never reaches the branch that sets the flag, and the `finally:` block then `shutil.rmtree`s the entire clone including `.git`. Uncommitted edits, unpushed commits, stashes, and the reflog all go at once — and with them the evidence needed to diagnose the failure that triggered the deletion, which makes the defect self-concealing. It compounds with aops_9c4e13a7: the stop-induced retry is guaranteed to fail at docker 125, and that guaranteed failure is precisely what routes through `fail()`.

Separately, a contributes_to edge pointing at a node that does not exist severs its source from any upstream chain while looking correctly wired in frontmatter. The larger problem is that three different duplicate-id counts are on record from three passes and nobody can currently say which is right, so any campaign sized against one of them is sized against a number that may be wrong by a factor of seven.

nodes.label: `update_body` is read-modify-write with no compare-and-swap: a concurrent writer's append is silently destroyed

contributes_to.justification: The target's statement is 'No silent divergence' — every write either persists AND is indexed, or fails loudly. A lost update is a write that persisted correctly and was then silently destroyed by a later write, with nothing failing loudly to either party; the target's own consequence prose ('data drift accumulates silently') names this outcome exactly. Probable rather than Certain because the literal clause the target leads with is 'no reported success without persistence', and here the report was accurate for the writer who won — the divergence is between writers, not between report and disk — and because the target's main single-write persistence branch advances independently of concurrency control.

nodes.consequence: PKB body content can be destroyed with no error, no warning, and no signal to either caller — the losing writer is never told, and the winning writer's call returns success. Detection is not built in anywhere on the path: the loss was caught on 2026-08-19 only because the writer happened to diff the result against an offline-constructed intended body, which is not a step any contract requires. The store is git-backed (`/home/nic/brain/.git`, auto-sync commits at roughly one-minute cadence), so a loss is *recoverable* once someone knows to look — but nothing makes them look: every auto-sync commit carries the identical message `auto: sync <timestamp>`, so a clobber is indistinguishable from a legitimate edit in the log, and a write/clobber pair landing inside one commit window leaves no committed intermediate state at all. Recoverable-but-undetected is the operating condition, and the graph is the single source of truth every planning decision reads.

contributes_to edges keyed `target:` never resolve — enumerate the dead population, then make the write path fail loudly

contributes_to.justification: Edges that resolve is the first thing this target's own reliability branch names. An unresolved contributes_to edge is a direct integrity defect in the ranking substrate every other planning decision reads from.

The goal's second half is that write results become trustworthy, not merely fast. A write that succeeds, emits no warning, and silently drops the edge is the same defect class as a write that times out after applying — and this one is self-seeding, so every brief written toward the goal can reproduce it.

nodes.consequence: Roughly 90 of 243 contributes_to edges in the store - 37% - are dead right now and invisibly so: each is severed from its target's upstream chain, its urgency stays pinned near 0.001, and it sorts below work that matters less. Because the write succeeds and no warning fires, an agent following the documented schema produces the defect, and an agent checking its work by re-reading the frontmatter confirms the defect as correct - so the error rate compounds with every brief pass rather than decaying. The largest single broken shape is the read projection copied back into a write, which is that loop in the data. Left alone, focus_score silently stops meaning what the whole planning model claims it means.
